title: Fibonacci Number
statement: Return the nth Fibonacci number, with F(0)=0 and F(1)=1.
explanation: Maintain the two most recent Fibonacci values and advance them n times.

title: Find Bottom Left Tree Value
statement: Return the leftmost value in the last row of a non-empty binary tree.
explanation: Traverse breadth-first, enqueueing right children before left children; the last visited node is the deepest row's leftmost node.

title: Find Largest Value in Each Tree Row
statement: Return the largest value in each row of a binary tree, ordered from the root row downward.
explanation: Use breadth-first traversal and compute the maximum among exactly the nodes in each level.

title: Detect Capital
statement: Return true if a word uses all capitals, all lowercase letters, or a capital only at its first character.
explanation: Check the three permitted capitalization patterns directly.

title: Longest Uncommon Subsequence I
statement: Return the length of the longest uncommon subsequence of two strings, or -1 if none exists.
explanation: If the strings are identical no uncommon subsequence exists; otherwise the longer entire string cannot be a subsequence of the shorter string.

title: Longest Uncommon Subsequence II
statement: Find the longest string in an array that is not a subsequence of any other string in the array.
explanation: Test candidates in descending length order and return the first candidate that is not a subsequence of any other entry.

title: Continuous Subarray Sum
statement: Determine whether the array contains a contiguous subarray of length at least two whose sum is a multiple of k.
explanation: Equal prefix-sum remainders imply the intervening sum is divisible by k; retain the earliest index for each remainder.

title: Longest Word in Dictionary through Deleting
statement: Find the longest dictionary word that can be formed by deleting characters from s; break ties by lexicographically smallest word.
explanation: Check each candidate with a two-pointer subsequence scan, then compare by length and lexicographic order.

title: Contiguous Array
statement: Return the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with equal numbers of zeros and ones.
explanation: Map each zero to -1 and each one to +1; equal prefix sums identify a balanced subarray.

title: Beautiful Arrangement
statement: Count permutations of 1 through n where at each position i, either the value divides i or i divides the value.
explanation: Fill positions in order, trying only unused values satisfying the divisibility condition and undoing each choice during backtracking.
